settings.title: India Has a Long History with Cotton
settings.text:
“It is so transparent and light that it looks as if one is in no dress at all but has only smeared the body with pure water.”

— Amir Khusrau, legendary Indian poet, describing Bengal muslin (cotton) c. 1320s

India first began producing cotton in the times of the Indus River Valley Civilization. Over centuries, they began to master its production, weaving the finest of cottons and applying the most intricate craft styles to it.

During their colonial rule, the British even banned Indian cotton to give their industries a lasting chance in global markets.

Recognizing the power of Indian cotton, Gandhi turned hand-spun and hand woven khadi cotton into a symbol of India’s resistance and self-reliance.

Praali brings together two of India’s greatest legacies: the cotton we’ve mastered for millennia and the practice of Yoga we gave the world in our clothing.

We specifically use cotton from the Better Cotton Initiative (BCI).

settings.title: The Body, As Understood by Ancient India is remarkable.
settings.text:
From Ayurveda and Yoga to the Natya Shastra and Kama Sutra, ancient Indian thinkers spent thousands of years contemplating how to nourish, heal, move, and inhabit our bodies.

All of Praali’s events and designs are inspired by these ancient Indian traditions and treatises.
